problemSolved: An LLM given the whole rule corpus (60 core rules + mode files + evidence/contract/interaction/critique prose + 1.4MB of CSV data) either burns context budget on every trivial task or starts ignoring the rules because there are too many to hold.
mechanism: A single machine-readable file (PIPELINE.json) declares exactly three things as `alwaysLoaded` (SKILL.md, v2/10-core.md, one mode file) and attaches a `reads` list to every pipeline step. Everything else (references/, data/, other mode files, benchmark-lab docs) is read only when its step is active and 'put down again' afterward (v2/README.md:32-33).
whyItWorks: It converts 'progressive disclosure' from an instruction the model has to remember into a lookup table a router can enforce mechanically: the step ID determines the read-list, not the model's judgement about what feels relevant.
outputImpact: Keeps the standing cost of every ordinary task to ~27KB (see CONTEXT-STRATEGY.md) regardless of project size, so a one-page brief and a nine-page site pay the same fixed overhead.
failureModes: Nothing stops an agent from reading the whole references/ tree anyway if it is curious and not explicitly told 'do not' each time — the discipline lives in SKILL.md prose, not in a hard gate.
Step->reads is declared for the v2/init/build/audit path only; ad-hoc tasks (COMPONENT, single AUDIT) fall back to informal routing in SKILL.md's routing table, which is less rigorously scoped.
testMethod: asserted only — no script checks that an agent actually limited its reads to the declared list for a given step; the discipline is prose plus the file layout making the wrong material inconvenient to reach.
sitesmithForm: Keep the always-loaded set to router + one universal rule file + one mode file; give every phase an explicit reads-manifest in a single machine-readable pipeline file so routing and context budget are the same artifact.

problemSolved: A plain top-3 BM25 search returns three rows that are all close to the query (by construction), so 'three directions' collapses to one idea restated three times — the repo's own measured legacy failure (nine subjects converging on one look).
mechanism: Loads a domain CSV (styles/colors/typography/etc.), scores it with hand-rolled BM25 (core.py:107-166) against the query plus dial-derived vocabulary (candidates.py:110-130), then greedily picks a seed (top match) and two more rows chosen to maximise minimum Jaccard-token distance from what is already chosen (candidates.py:228-249), with a same-project anti-repeat exclusion (candidates.py:186-224) and a confidence/'separation' verdict.
whyItWorks: As a search-diversity technique it is sound: it demonstrably returns three farther-apart rows than naive top-k, and it is honest about when the pool is thin ('confidence: low').
outputImpact: This is the mechanism most directly implicated in the benchmark loss named in the brief: a deterministic script pre-selects three canned 'Style Category' rows from a fixed vocabulary (glassmorphism, brutalism, minimalism, ...) and hands them to the model as 'candidates', which anchors the model's direction-writing to a menu of pre-existing named styles instead of reasoning from the evidence pack outward. The model that scored 59 was reasoning natively from evidence with no such menu; the mechanical generator scored 40 on the same brief.
failureModes: Directions get pulled toward whatever named style categories exist in styles.csv, which is a finite, dated vocabulary (the CSV was authored once, in 2024, for ui-ux-pro-max) — the exact opposite of 'evidence before design' that v2/05-evidence.md argues for.

detect_domain() (core.py:201-221) keyword-matches the query into one of 11 fixed domains; a subject whose vocabulary does not match any keyword list falls through to 'style' by default (core.py:221), silently mis-routing.

The three 'candidates' are optimized for mutual textual distance, not for fitness to the brief — 'furthest from the others' (candidates.py:228-237) is a proxy for structural difference, not a measure of it.
conflicts: Directly contradicts v2/05-evidence.md:16 ('nothing here decides a colour') in spirit: the search step runs before the direction is argued and its output is presented as the starting point for that argument, not as neutral research.
C-no-mechanical-creativity: this is the textbook case of a creative decision (which three visual identities to consider) moved into a script.
testMethod: asserted only — 'confidence' and 'separation' are computed and printed, but nothing checks that the chosen candidates actually produce better DIRECTION.md quality than an unaided model would.
sitesmithForm: Do not port a candidate-search-over-fixed-CSV step. If contrastive search on real content survives at all, use it only as optional background research the model may consult, never as the literal source of the three directions on the table; the model's own reasoning from EVIDENCE.md should generate the three directions.

sourcePath: skills/sitesmith/scripts/design_system.py:1-80 (1151 lines total); grep of v2/*.md and PIPELINE.json shows zero references to --design-system
problemSolved: Nothing in the current pipeline — this is dead code from the upstream ui-ux-pro-max-skill import, not called by any PIPELINE.json step or any v2/*.md instruction.
mechanism: `generate_design_system()` runs multi-domain BM25 searches (product/style/color/landing/typography) and a CSV-driven `ui-reasoning.csv` rule-matcher, then assembles a complete design-system recommendation procedurally, with a Master+Overrides persistence flow (search.py:19,140-152).
whyItWorks: N/A for this repo's actual build path — it is unreachable from the documented commands.
outputImpact: None on a normal build (never invoked), but it is 1151 lines of maintained surface area and a second, contradictory way to produce a 'design system' (fully mechanical) sitting next to the one the pipeline actually uses (30-contract.md, model-authored from the winning comp). A future maintainer or an agent exploring scripts/ could invoke it by hand and get v1-style mechanical output.
failureModes: Silent dead code: nothing marks it deprecated in-file; only absence of references proves it is unused.
If ever wired back in, it reproduces exactly the mechanical-creativity failure mode of direction-candidate-search, at the design-system-contract level instead of the direction level.
conflicts: Duplicates/contradicts v2/30-contract.md's explicit 'derived from the brief, not from this file' principle (30-contract.md:6-8).
sitesmithForm: Do not carry this file or its CLI flag forward. If any BM25/CSV lookup survives as an optional reference tool, keep it small and clearly labeled advisory-only.

problemSolved: A page designed from a brief alone can only look like its category, because a brief says function, not appearance; this is named as the root cause of nine subjects converging on one hero.
mechanism: A mandatory seven-section research artifact (artefacts, vocabulary, materials/surfaces, colour already true, constraints, references+anti-references, asset reality) written before any visual decision, sourced in a strict preference order (client-supplied > existing site > public trade material > category practitioners > 'stated as unknown'), with two required markers `(inferred)` / `(needed)` that later gates (production-gate.mjs) read.
whyItWorks: It forces the model to go find real, checkable specifics about the subject's actual world before generating anything, which is exactly the kind of grounding that makes an LLM produce a subject-specific idea instead of a category-average one — this is a 'make the model think better' mechanism, not a rule that replaces thinking.
outputImpact: Anti-references (05-evidence.md:69-80) are called out as doing more work than references — naming what must NOT be resembled, including 'the category default', directly targets house-style convergence.
failureModes: No mechanical check that EVIDENCE.md content actually influenced DIRECTION.md — the causal link is asserted by workflow order, not verified.
'Stated as unknown' (item 5 of the sourcing order) is honest but provides no forcing function against an agent that skips straight to invention when research is inconvenient.
testMethod: asserted only, via a 'when it is done' checklist (05-evidence.md:119-124) that a human/agent self-certifies; no script parses EVIDENCE.md content quality.
sitesmithForm: Keep as a required pre-direction research pass with the same seven sections and the same 'anti-references do more work than references' framing; this is a genuine lever on model creativity, not mechanical creativity.

problemSolved: Three comps that share a layout and differ only in hue are one direction rendered three times — round-8 testing showed three sites could pass an earlier five-axis check and a per-page critique and still read as one 'SiteSmith house style' (uppercase mono labels, hairlines, tabular figures, flat surfaces).
mechanism: DIRECTION.md/NOTE.md must declare a fixed, parseable record: 5 macro axes (composition, type, colour, imagery, rhythm) + 4 visual-grammar fields (surface, labels, figures, depth, each written as `<treatment> — <reason>`) + 3 integer dials. `direction-check.mjs` parses all three comps' NOTE.md, requires pairwise difference on >=3/5 macro axes including composition and >=2/4 grammar fields, then **renders each comp in a real browser and measures** ground luminance, display font family, image count, radius/size counts, mono-caps count, hairline count, tabular-nums count, shadow count — and fails the pair if the measured DOM disagrees with the declared axis (direction-check.mjs:179-221).
whyItWorks: Declaring difference in prose is cheap and gameable; measuring the rendered DOM against the declaration closes that gap. The known-bad round-8 recipe (4 specific device counts together) is hard-coded as an always-checked pattern (direction-check.mjs:208-219), so even a first-ever run on a clean install cannot slip past it.
requiredContext: playwright (optional — falls back to declared-axes-only check if absent)
outputImpact: This is the mechanism that actually enforces portfolio-level variety; without it 'three directions' is trivially satisfiable by writing three different adjectives.
failureModes: The macro-axis/grammar taxonomy is itself a fixed vocabulary (a closed list of named axis values the parser recognises) — a genuinely novel axis value that the regex classifiers in direction-fidelity.mjs don't recognise silently becomes 'unclassifiable' and is skipped rather than flagged as a gap in the taxonomy (direction-fidelity.mjs:274-347, 'notes' branch).
Requires playwright; degrades gracefully to declared-axes-only, which is real but weaker.
testMethod: real — actual rendering + DOM measurement, not self-report. This is the strongest verification mechanism in the repo.
sitesmithForm: Keep the declared-record + rendered-measurement double-check pattern, and keep the hard-coded 'known bad recipe' block list so novelty is enforced from a cold start, not only after the ledger accumulates history.

problemSolved: A declared direction can be real on paper and absent on screen: two actual pilots declared a dark ground, shipped it correctly behind `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, and both rendered light because Chromium's default scheme is light — every other gate in the repo passed (direction-fidelity.mjs:11-19).
mechanism: Renders the finished page with **no colour-scheme override** (matching what a screenshot/reviewer actually sees), then measures ground luminance (WCAG relative luminance formula, inlined), display font-family, asset area share of the first 1440x900 viewport, section 'bands' (distinct painted backgrounds), mono-caps/hairline/tabular-nums/shadow counts, and the declared `signature-selector`'s occupied area — and fails per-axis if the measurement contradicts the classified expectation from DIRECTION.md's prose (groundExpectation/typeExpectation/imageryExpectation/rhythmExpectation/surfaceExpectation/labelExpectation/figureExpectation/depthExpectation, lines 40-124).
whyItWorks: It measures the artifact a human reviewer actually judges (the default-scheme render), not the artifact the developer intended (the CSS source), closing a class of bug where 'the direction exists in the code but not on the page'.
requiredContext: the built page, reachable by URL
outputImpact: Catches a real, previously-shipped defect class (dark-mode-only direction) that no other check in the repo catches.
failureModes: Classifier regexes (e.g. groundExpectation's colour-word list, direction-fidelity.mjs:40-47) only recognise a fixed vocabulary of ground-words; a direction phrased outside that vocabulary is reported as a 'note' (unclassifiable) rather than a fail, silently reducing coverage.

A malformed DIRECTION.md (prose headings instead of the exact `- field: value` shape) fails the whole check before any visual judgement runs, and the failure message has had to be hardened twice because two separate builders wrote considered directions the parser could not read (direction-fidelity.mjs:259-271) — the mechanical parser is brittle to prose variation.
testMethod: real DOM measurement against a written contract; genuinely adversarial (the whole file exists because a real defect slipped past everything else).
sitesmithForm: Keep as the canonical 'does the shipped page match its stated direction' check, default-colour-scheme, no exceptions. Keep the fail-loud-on-malformed-record behavior, but consider a plain-English fallback path for axis values the classifier can't parse rather than only a 'note'.

problemSolved: A per-project novelty check cannot see repetition between projects, which is exactly where a house style forms — three unrelated sites can each pass their own direction-check and still all be the same design.
mechanism: One append-only ledger at `~/.sitesmith/direction-history.jsonl`, outside any single project's repo. `check` compares a new render's declared axes AND a rendered 'fingerprint' (ground luminance band, display-font class, imagery band, layout shape, a device-set built from measured counts) against every other project's entries, failing on: an exact fingerprint match, a hard-coded known-bad recipe (KNOWN_RECIPES, lines 29-38) matched even with an empty ledger, >=4 shared 'house-style devices' with any other project, or identical macro-axis words. `commit` (run during audit, on the finished site) re-checks and appends only on pass; the record stores no client URL (lines 9-12, 210).
whyItWorks: Cross-project memory is the only way to catch a style habit the model doesn't know it has, because within one project everything looks novel by definition.
requiredContext: ~/.sitesmith/direction-history.jsonl (grows across all projects on the machine)
outputImpact: Directly targets the brief's C-no-house-style constraint — this is the single most relevant piece of existing machinery for the stated problem ('three independently briefed sites converged on the same five moves').
failureModes: Ledger is local to one machine/home directory; it does not travel with the repo or team, so a different machine (or CI) starts with a colder history.

The 4-shared-device threshold and the specific KNOWN_RECIPES list are hand-tuned to the one failure episode that was actually measured (round 8) — a different house-style pattern with different measurable devices would not be caught until it, too, is observed and hard-coded.
testMethod: real — actual render fingerprinting against a persisted ledger, with a hard-coded floor that works even on a cold ledger.
sitesmithForm: Keep an append-only, no-URL, cross-project fingerprint ledger with both a fingerprint-similarity check and a fixed 'known recipe' block list seeded from whatever house-style patterns we ourselves measure.

problemSolved: Not one of nine legacy benchmark pages had a spacing scale or a type scale; every gap and font size was chosen ad hoc at the point of use, which is invisible in a diff but is exactly what makes a second page expensive (30-contract.md:27-34).
mechanism: DESIGN-SYSTEM.md is written **after** the winning comp is chosen, deriving its token values from that comp rather than imposing a pre-existing system (30-contract.md:6-8, 39-41). It has a mandatory fenced ```css contract``` block with 8 required token groups (spacing/type/shape/elevation/container/colour/families/motion) plus a documented 'one-off values' escape-hatch table for values the ramp genuinely can't carry (a decision, not a hidden default). `token-drift.mjs --contract` parses the contract's declared token values AND the one-off table, then scans every page's inline `<style>` for colour/length literals on 7 specific CSS properties, flags any that are neither a declared token value nor a listed one-off nor a small utility-value allowlist (`0, 1px, 50%, 100%, auto, none, inherit, 100vh/dvh/vw`), and separately reports declared-but-unused tokens.
whyItWorks: Ordering matters: writing the contract from the comp (not before it) is the concrete fix for the same convergence bug diagnosed in the direction lab — 'fixing tokens first... is how nine subjects converge on one look' (PIPELINE.json:9-11). The drift-checker then makes 'every value is a token or a documented exception' a mechanically enforced property instead of a style guideline nobody checks.
requiredContext: the built pages' inline CSS (or rendered DOM, for the general non-contract mode)
outputImpact: Converts 'consistent design system' from an aspiration into something a script actually verifies per page, while explicitly not banning composed one-off values (30-contract.md:53-68) — this is the rare token-discipline tool that distinguishes 'a decision' from 'the absence of one'.
failureModes: Only scans inline `<style>` blocks in static HTML (token-drift.mjs:55) — a page whose styling lives in separate CSS files, CSS-in-JS, or Tailwind utility classes is invisible to this checker unless it's pointed at the rendered/compiled output.

The one-off table is trusted verbatim (whatever a human/agent writes there is accepted) — nothing checks that a one-off is genuinely rare rather than a dumping ground; the file's own prose relies on a human-judged test ('can you write the reason in a clause') that no script enforces.
testMethod: real static/DOM analysis against a written contract, with a documented escape hatch.
sitesmithForm: Keep contract-after-direction ordering and the 8-required-group token block; keep a documented one-off table as the only escape hatch; extend the drift scanner to whatever styling mechanism the unified skill's stack actually uses (not just inline <style>).

problemSolved: A page can pass every accessibility/layout check and still not be a finished, honest page: a hatched placeholder box captioned 'Photograph would sit here' occupying half a viewport, and an empty coloured square standing in for a logo, both shipped in a set that passed every technical gate it had (production-gate.mjs:14-17).
mechanism: Regex-scans visible text (script/style/comments stripped, lines 66-69) for placeholder language (lines 24-42) and dummy identifiers — example.com, 555 phone numbers, 'Anytown', reserved test emails (lines 46-55); flags empty elements standing in for a brand mark (lines 174-185); requires every img/inline-svg to carry a `data-asset` id present in ASSET-MANIFEST.md with state `ready` (lines 265-343); in mode E, extracts commerce claims (prices, review counts, star ratings, delivery/warranty/certification claims, lines 281-292) and blocks any that cannot be traced to EVIDENCE.md or a `data-source` attribute (lines 294-324); requires a borrowed customer/partner logo wall to name every mark via alt/aria-label and to be traceable to EVIDENCE.md, never a 'substitute' state (lines 191-237); requires at least one journeys/*.spec.mjs to exist (lines 492-498). Draft mode reports only; `--production` exits non-zero on any blocking finding.
whyItWorks: It operationalizes 'a website is not done when checks pass' into checks a script CAN run: honesty about what is real (assets, claims, endorsements) is exactly the category of defect invisible to accessibility/layout tooling but catchable by text/DOM pattern matching plus a manifest cross-reference.
requiredContext: the built pages (files or a rendered URL)
outputImpact: This is the mechanism most directly responsible for catching fabricated-authenticity failures (fake testimonials, invented metrics, unlicensed customer logos) that the brief's anti-slop framing treats as absolute red lines.
failureModes: Static scan of markup only by default; a page whose content is built by client-side script is invisible unless a URL is passed so the rendered DOM is read instead (documented explicitly at lines 76-82 as a real blind spot, with the fix being 'pass a URL', not 'trust the script').
The placeholder/dummy-identifier regex lists are a closed, hand-maintained set (lines 24-55) — a new placeholder phrasing not on the list passes silently.

Commerce-claim tracing does simple substring/normalised matching against EVIDENCE.md text (lines 296-306); a price stated in a different format (e.g. '£1,299' vs '1299 GBP') may not match and produce a false positive block.
testMethod: real regex/DOM scan against a manifest and an evidence file; genuinely adversarial (comments explain three previously-shipped defects the tool now catches).
sitesmithForm: Keep the placeholder-language, dummy-identifier, unmanifested-asset and traceable-commerce-claim checks as a distinct 'is it finished/honest' gate, separate from the accessibility/layout gate; keep draft-vs-production modes so the same tool serves both in-progress and release use.

problemSolved: Across the nine legacy benchmark pages there are zero <script> tags: every interactive state (a product page's price, a dashboard's filters, a form's step indicator, a keyboard-shortcut legend) is drawn correctly and never reachable (40-interaction.md:10-14).
mechanism: INTERACTIONS.md enumerates every primary action with an observably-checkable success/failure outcome, per-surface reachable states, and a keyboard/focus map. At least one Playwright journey per surface (journeys/<name>.spec.mjs) must assert four specific things: something observably changed, the change is announced (role=status/alert/focus move, not just a visual change), a deliberate failure path is handled and attached to its field, and the same outcome is reachable by keyboard with visible focus (40-interaction.md:115-129). `journey.mjs` is a thin runner: spawns each spec as a child process with a 120s timeout, reports pass/fail per file, non-zero exit on any failure. `production-gate.mjs --production` independently fails if journeys/ is empty (production-gate.mjs:492-498).
whyItWorks: Forcing an assertion on 'something changed AND is announced AND has a failure path AND is keyboard-reachable' is a much higher bar than 'the click handler didn't throw' and catches the exact defect class the file was written against (styled-but-unwired states).
requiredContext: v2/40-interaction.md (once, at end of init / start of build)
a running dev server at the journey's BASE url
outputImpact: Converts 'the UI has states' from a visual claim into a behavioral one that a script actually exercises against the live page.
failureModes: Journeys are hand-written per project — there is no generator, so journey coverage quality depends entirely on whether the model wrote a journey that actually exercises the four required properties versus one that merely clicks and checks nothing changed to a low bar.
120s per-spec timeout (journey.mjs:36) is a fixed budget that may be wrong for a slow dev server or a journey with many steps; there's no per-journey override in the runner itself.
testMethod: real browser automation against the live page; the runner reports actual pass/fail, not a self-report.
sitesmithForm: Keep the four-part assertion contract (changed / announced / failure-path / keyboard-path) as the definition of a valid journey, and keep 'no journeys/ = production gate fails' as a hard floor.

problemSolved: Merging 'does it work' and 'is it any good' is how a green PASS came to be read as 'this is good' — a page can pass every mechanical check and still be indistinguishable from four hundred others (v2/00-done.md:199-200).
mechanism: The technical gate (verify/token-drift/production-gate/journey) must be green before the visual critique runs at all — a broken layout cannot be assessed for art direction because every criticism collapses into the break (50-critique.md:14-16). The visual critique itself is a 7-criterion rubric (direction, specificity-to-subject, type, colour, assets, hierarchy, production-readiness) scored 1-10 on screenshots only (never source), with a mandatory one-sentence 'primary criticism' answered before scores are seen. If that sentence names the generic-AI-template failure, the gate fails regardless of numeric scores (50-critique.md:99-112) — a good average cannot hide the one failure the whole layer exists to catch. Specificity is capped at 3 if the page 'could be a different company in the same category' with only copy changed (50-critique.md:52-54).
whyItWorks: Separating the floor (mechanical, no opinion) from the ceiling (judgement, opinionated) stops technical green from being mistaken for creative good, and the primary-criticism test is a targeted trap specifically for the failure mode the brief cares about (genericness/house-style), not a generic quality score that could average it away.
requiredContext: v2/50-critique.md, read once after the technical gate is green
screenshots at 3 widths x 2 colour schemes plus the 3 rejected direction comps
outputImpact: The specificity cap-at-3 rule and the primary-criticism generic-tell test are the two places in the whole repo that most directly operationalize 'would a designer say a machine made this' as a scored, failable check rather than a vibe.
failureModes: The rubric depends on the reviewer being honest and genuinely independent of the builder — for an ordinary single-site build this is one agent doing both the building and the reviewing in sequence, which is a materially weaker guarantee than the benchmark-lab version (see critique-gate mechanism, which does enforce independence, but only applies lab-side).
'Take the logo and copy off, could this be a different company' is a judgement call with no mechanical proxy in the ordinary (non-lab) path — nothing computes it.
testMethod: asserted for ordinary single-site work (human/agent self-scores against the rubric); enforced mechanically only in the benchmark-lab variant (critique-gate.mjs).
sitesmithForm: Keep the hard order (technical green first, then visual judgement) and the primary-criticism generic-tell test with its scores-cannot-override-it rule; keep the specificity-cap-at-3 rubric item as the concrete operationalization of 'genuinely about this subject'.

problemSolved: A blind review that is only described in prose is a blind review that will not actually happen; specifically: one reviewer instead of two, the key opened before both reviews lock, or a good average hiding the one criticism that matters (critique-gate.mjs:10-14).
mechanism: Enforces, by parsing frontmatter + hashing review bodies: the reviewer is not the build agent (`built-by` vs `reviewer-id`, lines 145-156); both reviews are bound to the same brief/rubric/screenshot-set by sha256 (lines 158-166); labels are opaque (regex-checked against the subject name, lines 170-173); >=2 independent named reviewers (lines 175-183); each review's body-hash matches its recorded sha256, i.e. wasn't edited post-lock (lines 191-195); the sealed key's `opened` timestamp is strictly after every reviewer's `locked` timestamp (lines 204-220); a generic-template tell is scanned sentence-by-sentence across the WHOLE review body, not just the headline answer, with an explicit negation/contrast grammar (NEGATORS, lines 74-93) so a reviewer praising the page ('the difference between a foundry and a template') isn't misread as raising the failure; median production-readiness must reach 8, no criterion below floor 4, and a >=3-point reviewer disagreement is reported as a finding rather than averaged away (lines 246-259). This entire file is explicitly scoped to benchmark-lab work, not ordinary customer builds (v2/50-critique.md:141-155, PIPELINE.json:346).
whyItWorks: Every check targets a specific, named way the ceremony has actually failed before (self-review, post-hoc score editing, key opened early, a burying of the real criticism in prose) rather than a generic 'be rigorous' instruction — this is what makes a described process into an enforced one.
requiredContext: two CRITIQUE-<reviewer>.md files with the specified frontmatter
outputImpact: This is real, portable verification-ceremony machinery — but it is scoped by the source itself to benchmark/portfolio work, not ordinary single-site delivery, which the rebuild should preserve rather than universalize.
failureModes: The negation-detection regex list (NEGATORS, lines 74-93) is a hand-built grammar over English contrast constructions; a real reviewer using an unanticipated phrasing to praise the page could still be misread as raising the generic-template failure.

Nothing stops a human/agent from fabricating two 'independent' reviewer identities that are both actually one agent role-playing — the sha256/timestamp discipline proves the ceremony's mechanics happened, not that the two judgements were cognitively independent.
conflicts: Scope conflict risk if ported carelessly: applying this ceremony's overhead to every ordinary customer build would be disproportionate — the source itself gates this to lab/portfolio work only.
testMethod: real — hash + timestamp + regex verification of an actual artifact trail, not self-report.
sitesmithForm: Keep the ceremony (independent reviewers, sealed key, sha256-locked reviews, generic-tell sentence scan with negation handling, disagreement-is-a-finding) available as an explicit opt-in for portfolio/benchmark claims; do not make it a default step of an ordinary single-site build.

problemSolved: Individual page critique and individual direction-fidelity can each pass while a set of sites still reads as one studio's work: three pilots with different evidence packs, different modes, and different chosen directions all rendered off-white grounds within a 0.031 luminance band, letterspaced uppercase mono labels, hairline borders, and sub-5%-of-viewport line-drawing imagery — every existing single-site gate passed (portfolio-diversity.mjs:11-16).
mechanism: Given 2+ rendered URLs, measures each (ground colour/luminance, display font family, asset share, mono-caps/hairline/tabular/shadow counts, a first-screen 'layout signature') then checks the SET: any two-or-more sites whose ground luminance falls within a 0.18 band are one palette family (line 35); any device used by MORE than 2-of-3 sites is flagged as belonging to the portfolio rather than any one site (sharedDeviceLimit=2, line 37); if no site in the set clears 12% imagery share of its first screen, imagery is never load-bearing anywhere (imageryLeaderMin=12, line 40); 2+ sites sharing the same coarse layout signature fail (layoutSignatureLimit=2, line 42); and display-face diversity is checked directly (all sites must use distinct display families, lines 116-120).
whyItWorks: It measures a property (set-level sameness) that no single-site gate can see by construction — this is the direct mechanical answer to the brief's C-no-house-style constraint, and it is explicitly lab-scoped rather than run per customer site.
outputImpact: This is the most literal existing implementation of 'catch a house style forming across independently-briefed outputs' — directly on-point for the rebuild's stated constraint.
failureModes: Thresholds (0.18 luminance band, sharedDeviceLimit=2, imageryLeaderMin=12%) are hand-tuned to the one measured round-8 episode; a different, differently-shaped house-style convergence (e.g. shared motion patterns, shared copy cadence) is invisible to this specific measurement set.

Only runs when explicitly invoked on a multi-site set — nothing in the ordinary single-site pipeline ever triggers it, so it provides zero protection unless someone remembers to run it before a portfolio claim (v2/50-critique.md:141-155 states this explicitly as by-design scope, not an oversight).
testMethod: real cross-site DOM measurement and comparison; the mechanism this whole autopsy's commissioning benchmark (round 8, mini-1 vs LLM) is itself an instance of the failure this gate targets.
sitesmithForm: Keep as a mandatory pre-showcase/portfolio gate (not a per-site step): measure ground-family clustering, shared-device-across-set counts, whether imagery is load-bearing anywhere in the set, layout-signature collisions, and display-face diversity across whatever multi-output claim the rebuilt skill ever makes.

problemSolved: A gate that silently 'did not run' and still prints PASS is worse than no gate — a fresh install without @axe-core/playwright installed reported 'axe violations: not run' and passed, and nobody looked twice because not-run reads as fine, not failed (verify.mjs:264-269). Separately: layouts that fit only under the developer's own system font shipped broken on Linux CI twice (+10px, +20px overflow) invisible to any element-by-element scan (verify.mjs:42-50).
mechanism: Screenshots at 3 widths (default 375/768/1440) with devicePixelRatio 2; captures console errors and failed network requests; checks every same-origin link for HTTP >=400 or a literal `href="#"` placeholder; reads the raw HTML source (not the parsed DOM) for structural defects — missing doctype/html/head/body/lang attribute/h1-count/main-landmark — because the browser's DOM auto-repairs a missing root element, hiding the defect from anything that inspects document.* (verify.mjs:169-186); runs axe-core in BOTH light and dark colour schemes (verify.mjs:218-230, because a palette passing in light routinely fails in dark and 'testing one and inferring the other is how that ships'); an explicit `--font-stress` mode swaps in a deliberately wide font stack before measuring overflow; and treats a MISSING axe scan as a blocking failure unless `--no-axe` is explicitly passed, which prints exactly what waiving it costs (verify.mjs:270-272, 298-303).
whyItWorks: Every check here targets a real, previously-shipped, previously-invisible defect class named in the code's own comments — this is post-mortem-driven tooling, not speculative coverage.
requiredContext: playwright + @axe-core/playwright installed in the project under test
a reachable URL (dev server or built output)
outputImpact: Fail-closed defaults (axe missing = block, not pass) and testing the actual HTML source for structural defects (not just the live DOM) are both mechanisms that specifically prevent a false-green signal.
failureModes: Requires the target project to have playwright installed; on a fresh project with no dependencies yet, verify.mjs cannot run at all and the fallback is 'open the page manually and report the mechanical verdict is missing' (SKILL.md:181-182) — a real gap for the very first iteration of a build.

The `--no-axe` preview mode exists for iteration speed but is explicitly documented as unable to ever produce a release verdict (SKILL.md:86-87) — a discipline that depends on the agent actually re-running the full check before claiming done, not on the tool preventing a false claim.
testMethod: real browser automation, real axe-core accessibility engine, real HTTP status checks against actual same-origin links.
sitesmithForm: Keep dual-colour-scheme axe scanning, fail-closed-on-missing-axe-scan, raw-source structural checks (not DOM-only), and the font-stress overflow mode; keep the explicit preview-vs-release distinction (fast/waived vs canonical/enforced).

problemSolved: v1 issued global rules and then contradicted itself when context demanded otherwise (a mandatory one-radius lock in one file, 'identical radius everywhere is a defect' in another) because it tried to answer once for every kind of page.
mechanism: Two independent routing questions asked in a fixed order: which of 3 modes (Marketing/E-commerce/Product UI) is THIS PAGE (decided per page, not per project — a shop's About page is marketing, its order admin is product UI, SKILL.md:28), then which of 5 tasks (SETUP/NEW/REDESIGN/COMPONENT/AUDIT) applies. Mode files state outcomes, deliberately not defaults: 'there is no default hero, no mode radius and no mode spacing, because a named default is what gets reached for' (v2/README.md:81-82).
whyItWorks: Separating 'what kind of page is this' from 'what task am I doing' lets one rule set hold both without contradiction, and refusing to state a default (only an outcome per mode) removes the exact thing an agent reaches for under time pressure.
requiredContext: one v2/modes/*.md file, selected by the mode decision
outputImpact: Prevents the specific v1 self-contradiction pattern (global rule + contextual override fighting each other) by asking the context question first and only loading one answer.
failureModes: The mode decision itself is unassisted judgement with no mechanical check — nothing verifies that a page was routed to the correct mode, so a genuinely ambiguous page (e.g. a pricing page that is part-marketing, part-product-configurator) has no tie-breaking mechanism beyond agent discretion.
sitesmithForm: Keep per-page (not per-project) mode routing as a first decision, and keep mode files as outcome statements rather than default values, to avoid re-introducing a 'reached-for default'.
